LIFE IN THE HEART OF CENTRES 


MISSION OF THE MONTREAL YMCA 


“The Montreal YMCA is a partnership of volunteers and staff committed to the fulfillment of people in 
spirit, mind and body and to the development of self-reliance in the individual and the community. 


Through its actions, programs and services, the Montreal YMCA reflects the needs and aspirations of 
communities and works with individuals, local communities and communities in developing countries 


in achieving social justice and control of their environments.”

ITREAL YMCA 


MESSAGE FROM THE CHAIRMAN OF THE BOARD OF . 
DIRECTORS AND PRESIDENT & CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER 


The Montreal YMCA celebrated its 150th anniversary this year, joining 
the ranks of the major institutions that formed Montreal's character and 
landscape. For the past 150 years, the Montreal YMCA has provided 
Montrealers from all walks of life with the support, training and services 
they need to lead a richer and more dynamic life. 


Testimonials to the importance of the YMCA’s role in this city poured in 
throughout the year, and we continue to receive many donations toward 
the revitalization of the Downtown YMCA. Furthermore, we renewed our 
agreement with Centraide for three years, which provides invaluable 
support for our community programs. Centres were also eager to remind 
local community members that the YMCA’s doors are wide open, in 
addition to thanking them for their confidence and support. 


As luck would have it, our year of celebrations coincided with the 
International Year of Volunteers. We could not have wished for a better 
opportunity to pay tribute to the thousands of volunteers who have passed 
through our doors and our lives in the last 150 years to make the 
Montreal YMCA what it is today. 


In keeping with its prevention and integration goals, the YMCA continued 
to set up new programs this year and build new partnerships with the 
solid backing of its volunteers and staff. The pages that follow clearly 
illustrate the important role that the ten YMCA centres play in the 
everyday life and hearts of people in the Greater Montreal Area. 


Our future has never looked so bright. The soundness of the YMCA and 
its finances are a source of freedom and new opportunity for us. We 
intend to make the most of our situation by expanding and improving our 
programs and services. 


In this anniversary year, we sensed more vitality than ever before on the 
part of our volunteers, staff, the Board of Directors and the Montreal 
YMCA Foundation in their dedication to the ongoing improvement of the: 
YMCA. Thank you all. 


Happy 150"! 


Wad wl 


3 Paul Dunne Michael Weil 
: Chairman of the Board President & CEO 


LIFE IN THE HEART OF CENTRES 


THE DOWNTOWN YMCA IS OPEN. WIDE OPEN. 


The Downtown YMCA has been totally revitalized! It now features leading-edge equipment and larger 
premises that enable hundreds of volunteers and staff to offer health programs, physical activities, as 
well as educational and community services that meet members’ expectations, in addition to the needs 
of youth, families, seniors and the underprivileged downtown. 


The same spirit and warmth that have pervaded the Montreal YMCA for the past 150 years live on in 
the completely new and more spacious facilities. 


As a unique crossroads where thousands of people who reflect modern-day Montreal converge, the 
Montreal YMCA’s new facilities are concrete proof of its solid roots in the downtown area, community 
involvement and openness. Our message obviously came through loud and clear to the people who 
live and work downtown, because membership in the centre has doubled in the past five months! 


DU PARC YMCA 


Partnerships in Action 
For the past several years, the community sector of the Du Pare YMCA has taken a partnership-driven 
approach. The results speak for themselves... 


Affordable rental housing is in short supply in the increasingly popular Plateau Mont-Royal area, 
which has resulted in the exclusion of low-income individuals. Les Loges Mile-End (a public housing 
project created by the YMCA) the Centre d’action socio-communautaire de Montréal and L’Hirondelle 
(an organization that offers services for immigrants) have renovated two old buildings and created a 
total of 37 new dwellings. Their action encouraged tenants to develop a mutual assistance network. 
which has helped a number of them feel less isolated. 


The Alternative Suspension program, which offers support to youth who are temporarily suspended 
from school, has expanded significantly to encompass secondary schools in the community and 
parents, as well as the St-Louis du Pare CLSC, job-search organizations, several trade schools and 
some local private companies. 


GUY-FAVREAU_ YMCA 


At the Heart of the Community 

Diversity is the watchword in this area shared by the Chinese community, low-income individuals, 
seniors and business people. The centre has increased its initiatives to ensure that everyone feels at 
home in the neighbourbood. 


This year, the Guy-Favreau YMCA opened its doors free of charge to more than a dozen organizations, 
including the Sports Association for the Blind, Centre de jour Roland-Major, Faubourgs CLSC, Chinese 
Family Services, Centres de la petite enfance (daycares) and Action Centre-ville. 


Furthermore, the Guy-Favreau YMCA launched a physical fitness program for 
seniors who live in Habitations Jeanne-Mance with support from the YMCA 
endowment fund and in cooperation with the Faubourgs CLSC. The program, — 
which was designed to increase awareness of the benefits of physical activity — 
among seniors, also helped diminish their feelings of isolation and loneliness. 


HOCHELAGA-MAISONNEUVE YMCA 


Exploring Life on the Prairies 

As part of the YMCA’s Jouth Exchange Canada program, ten youth aged 13 to 
17 from the Hochelaga-Maisonneuve Youth Services Co-op were twinned with 
students from a school in the Town of Eston, Saskatchewan with a population of 
900. 


For some teens, the journey to the Prairies was their first “real” trip. Their 
J , 
enthusiasm combined with the warm welcome they received helped surmount 
language barriers. so they could make the most of 
haere J 
this opportunity to explore a different world full of 
grain elevators, museums and wapiti ranches. 


LIFE IN THE HEART OF CENTRES 


Our teens then worked relentlessly to organize a warm welcome of their own for 
their newfound Saskatchewan friends, and the Loblaw’s supermarket on Rachel 
St. generously contributed food toward their meals. The youth were eager to 
impress their visitors and organized visits to the Biodome, Botanical Gardens, 
Pointe-a-Calliére Museum, Chinatown, Mount Royal Park, etc... 


mY --. Ft 


The experience proved so enriching that they are all keen to relive the same 
adventure next year! 


NDG YMCA 


Breaking Boundaries through Basketball 

The third annual March Madness basketball tournament this year brought 
together 32 men’s and women’s teams in categories ranging in age from 10 years 
old and up. The aim of the friendly tournament is to break boundaries by 
enabling youth from all cultural backgrounds to get to know each other in a fun 
setting. More than 150 volunteers and staff worked to organize the event, which 
also helped raise funds for the NDG Y Teen Centre. 


The teen centre has 650 participants from 20 different cultures. After the 
centre opened in 1995, it quickly became the meeting place of choice for 
neighbourhood teens, who are naturally attracted by the sports, but also by the 
counselling and mentoring services. In addition, the centre offers numerous 
special activities, such as: Black History Month, the Unloading Zone (an anger 
management program implemented in local primary and secondary schools), 
support for Chez mes amis (a local community restaurant), and a food drive for 
the NDG Food Depot in association with the neighbourhood police. 


LIFE IN THE HEART OF CENTRES 


POINTE-ST-CHARLES YMCA 


A Helping Hand 
The Pointe-Saint-Charles YMCA offers youth aged 6 to 35 help with homework, going back to school 
or employment training. 


The Help with Homework Club has some fifty children at the primary level and fifteen secondary 
students in their first year. This program to promote academic achievement brings together numerous 
partners, including the St-Gabriel and Jeanne-Leber Schools, Westmount Park, the Montreal Museum 


of Fine Arts, Eco-Quartier, Share the Warmth, the Pointe-St-Charles Historical Society, the CSDM and 
CSEM, as well as the Ministére de l’Education. 


Another partnership between the YMCA and the City of Montreal, Government of Quebec, RESO (a 
network for the economic and social revitalization of Southwest Montreal) and C.A.F.E. Paradoxe 
made it possible to convert the centre’s former pool into an introductory performing arts school. The 
aim of the school, which is managed by C.A.F.E. Paradoxe, is to encourage young adults between the 
ages of 16 and 35 to return to school or take employment training. 


SAINT-LAURENT YMCA 


Saturday Program for Youth 

The Norgate-Crevier area in Saint-Laurent is one of the most underprivileged neighbourhoods on the 
Island of Montreal. As a result of social problems, lack of supervised activities asi prevention in the 
area, the Saint-Laurent YMCA launched a pilot project with the local municipality and the 
Enfant-Soleil School for youth aged 10 to 12. 


The aim of the program is to help youth become aware of their talents and develop their critical 
thinking. It is also designed to enable youth to develop key social skills, such as self-esteem, 
self-confidence, respect for others and a sense of responsibility with a view to preventing juvenile 
detente and drug or alcohol abuse. The program also focuses on developing leade ship skills. To 
achieve a multiplier effect 12 youth are encouraged to exert a positive influence on their peers. 


The Samedis ensoleillés program, which was originally planned for the school year only, was extended 
throughout the summer. The program is successful because its focus on arts and science is well 
balanced with leisure and sports. 


WEST ISLAND YMCA 


Jobs Wanted 

Youth aged 12 to 17 with no experience or trade seeks job... It’s hard to do on your own. That’s why 
the West Island Youth Services Co-op set up a program designed for youth who are faced with the 
harsh realities of the working world. They are given two days of training to help them prepare for 
various jobs, including baby-sitting, window washing, house painting, lawn mowing, and so on. 


SS Rees 


The youth are separated into three committees: finance, personnel and | 
promotion. Members must volunteer a minimum of two hours per week to the | : 
organization by helping to find employers, etc... In addition, members who 
obtain a contract through the co-op must pay 10% of their contract earnings 
toward the organization’s operations. 


Sponsored by the YMCA, Saint-Louis CLSC, Carrefour jeunesse emploi de 
Dorval (a job marketplace for youth) and the MUC Police, the co-op helps teens 
become more resourceful and develop their entrepreneurial skills. 


WESTMOUNT YMCA 


Weight Training for Seniors 

After obtaining her certification as a Fitness Instructor five years ago, Yaffa 
Gruia decided to volunteer in the weight-training room and take her knowledge 
of physiology one step further. As part of the process, she realized how 
important exercise is for seniors and decided to set 
up a customized weight-training program for 
people over fifty. 


LIFE IN THE HEART OF CENTRES 


Today, Yaffa leads a group of volunteers who provide guidance to seniors 
interested in improving their overall health and fitness. Each volunteer works 
with two participants at a time on a safe and effective weight-training program. 
Participants also receive awareness packages with information on proper diet, 
fluid intake, stretching, cardiovascular fitness, posture, and so on. 


The program offered by Yaffa and her team is a resounding success on all 
fronts. Aside from the obvious physical rewards, there are psychological and 
social benefits to the program as well, since it helps create a true sense of 
belonging in a very supportive and stimulating environment. 


KAMP _KANAWANA 


Once again this year, the camp welcomed people from the YMCA and from 
numerous other organizations as well, including the Allan Memorial Institute 
and several Montreal school boards. During the summer, a total of 

1,220 campers between the ages of 3 and 60 thoroughly enjoyed themselves in 
our summer camp and rental programs alone. 


The YMCA financial assistance program helped 27 children from low-income 
families enjoy the Kamp Kanawana experience. Total funding for the children 
amounted to $13,000. 


At the end of the summer, all remaining food from the kitchen, as well as any 
unclaimed clothing from the lost-and-found were donated to Le Bon Dieu dans 


la Rue. 


Big news! We are currently working on organizing the first annual “Kamper 
Reunion” over the holiday season. 


LIFE IN THE HEART OF CENTRES 


INTERNATIONAL PROGRAMS 


Companeros sin Fronteras 

This year, the YMCA focused its efforts on international development initiatives. The Montreal YMCA 
sent three young women to El Salvador, Nicaragua and Ecuador for six months as part of a project 
backed by CIDA (Canadian International Development Agency). 


Following the earthquakes in El Salvador in early 2001, Montreal YMCA centres jointly raised $6,920 
to help finance local relief and reconstruction projects. 
me : 


_ 1 


Here at home, International Programs offered a series of workshops to YMCA staff and volunteers on 
international development issues. 


In November 2000, the Montreal YMCA awarded its Peace Medallion to nine individuals and groups 
who distinguished themselves as peacemakers in action. 


THE MONTREAL YMCA CELEBRATES ITS 150TH ANNIVERSARY 


In addition to the opening of the Downtown YMCA, this very special year has been celebrated in 
numerous other ways. 


Youth Variety Show 

Some sixty youth from YMCA centres throughout the city staged a variety show that included singers, 
dancers, rappers and musicians. The show was first presented at Concordia University’s Oscar 
Peterson Concert Hall, then later at Parc Marguerite-Bourgeoys as part of the entertainment activities 
for Montreal’s Tour de Vile. Some 35,000 avid cyclists had the opportunity to see our youths’ talent. 


YMCA Participates in the St. Patrick’s Day Parade 

The Montreal YMCA proudly extended its 150th anniversary celebrations onto St. Catherine Street at 
the annual St. Patrick’s Day Parade that features all major Montreal area institutions. The YMCA 
float, which was designed by a group of Concordia University students, won the “Best Amateur Float 
Award”. 


Commemorative Stamp 

The Canada Post stamp launched this year to commemorate the 150th anniversary of the YMCA in 
Canada actually marked the opening of the Montreal YMCA, since it was the first centre to open in 
North America.

FOUNDATION 


MESSAGE FROM THE CHAIRMAN OF THE BOARD OF 
DIRECTORS AND PRESIDENT OF THE MONTREAL YMCA 
FOUNDATION 


The role of the Foundation is to ensure long-term funding for the 
Montreal YMCA so all of our centres can play a front-line role in 
the community, while ensuring access for all to our programs. 


This year marked the end of our ambitious revitalization campaign. 
The banners on the building’s fagade say it all. We have achieved 
our goal! With the determination of our Campaign Committee and 
generosity of more than 1,600 donors, we were able to collect the 


funds we needed to build the new Downtown YMCA. 


As soon as the campaign was over, the Foundation began 
consolidating the long-term financial situation of the Montreal 
YMCA. The Foundation intends to increase its Endowment fund, 
which currently stands at $3.5 million, by recruiting new 
participants. The fund will be managed by the new Greater 
Montreal Foundation. 


Given the role of the Montreal YMCA in the region, it seemed 

q completely natural to lend our support to the implementation of 
this new tool to assist the people of Greater Montreal. In exchange, 
the Greater Montreal Foundation will enable the YMCA to reduce 
its capital management costs, thereby increasing the amounts paid 
out every year in support of various causes. 


We wish to thank the members of our Board. all the volunteers who 
worked on the revitalization campaign, as well as the Foundation’s 

personnel. The YMCA’s community action largely depends on their 
effectiveness and dedication. 


Claude A. Garcia Marcel Coté 
Chairman of the Board President
